name: Z-Boat 1800 HS
notes: Modeled small-class survey ASV (~1.9 m LOA). All figures are simulation estimates for behavior study, not vendor specifications.

hull.air_draft_source: THE BOAT'S HEIGHT, TAKEN WHOLE (2026-10-12): the maker's User's Guide (January 2017) gives 'Boat height 1.1 m, depending on configuration' (p. 9). The 0.12 m draft is not taken off it, because the antennas vary by configuration and the larger figure is the safe one. A bridge or overhead line charted lower than this plus planning.overhead_clearance_m (1.0 m, ESTIMATED: US charts give vertical clearance at mean high water, and a spring tide, a surge or her pitch takes some of it) is a keep-out for her.

power.source: ESTIMATED (2026-10-11) from the maker's User's Guide (January 2017): start 26-27 V, the default 23 V alarm says the boat should be brought back to shore, 18 V is complete failure, the steering first (p. 8); 'operating endurance between charges ranges from 30 minutes to 90 minutes' on three 24 V 10 Ah NiMH packs (p. 13), 'up to 4.5 hours, depending on configuration' (p. 3), survey speed 3-3.5 kn. The drain (V/s at idle, and added at full speed) is fitted to 90 minutes from full to the 23 V alarm at survey speed (3 kn), 0.36 V/h of it the hotel load: 49 minutes at 6 kn, and 3.6 h to 18 V. It was 0.0006 / 0.0025, which reached the alarm in 32 minutes at survey speed. NiMH holds its voltage on a plateau and falls at the end, so a straight-line drain is an estimate - replace it with a measured discharge.
